title: FBN Inventory Reimbursement Terms
content:
These terms govern reimbursements of Fulfilled by Northloop (FBN) inventory: units lost or damaged while in Northloop's custody, inbound shipments received short, customer returns never received and lost removal shipments.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses of these terms are **no longer in force** and have been superseded by the current basis for the cases concerned. They are reproduced here as text that no longer decides any case:

> Northloop reimburses units lost or damaged in its custody.

> A warehouse loss claim is filed no later than the warehouse loss claim window counted in calendar days from the inventory adjustment date.

> An inbound shortage claim (units expected less units received on a shipment line) may be filed only after the inbound reconciliation wait and within the inbound shortage claim window, both counted in calendar days from the receipt date of that line.

The filing limit that the second clause set — a window counted in calendar days from the inventory adjustment date, inclusive of its last day — is withdrawn with that clause and is no longer in force. The program figures named in these clauses remain the figures of each program.

## Clauses in force

1. **Automatic reimbursement.** A lost-in-warehouse or damaged-in-warehouse adjustment not found within the auto-reimburse days is reimbursed automatically.
2. **Customer return not received.** A customer-return-not-received claim may be filed after the return wait and within the return claim window, both counted from the buyer refund date of the order, and only when no restock of that order exists.
3. **Lost removal shipment.** A lost removal claim may be filed within the removal claim window counted from the removal order's creation.
4. **Valuation.** Each unit is valued at the declared unit cost on the SKU's latest inbound receipt, capped at the program's reimbursement unit value cap. The amount reimbursed is the units multiplied by the lower of that declared unit cost and the cap, rounded to the cent.
5. **No second reimbursement.** Units already reimbursed on the same source object are never reimbursed again.
6. **Found units.** When reimbursed units are found and found-inventory reversal is in force for the program, the reimbursement is reversed.

## The same source object

The units already reimbursed on a source object are the units on earlier reimbursements that share all three of: the same loss kind; the same source reference — the inventory adjustment for a warehouse loss or damage, the inbound shipment for an inbound shortage, the order for a customer return not received, the removal order for a lost removal shipment; and the same SKU. This is read from Northloop's reimbursement records, not from the seller's account of what was paid.

| Earlier reimbursement on record (hypothetical) | Same source object as a new claim for 5 units of SKU A on adjustment 1? |
|---|---|
| 3 units, warehouse loss, adjustment 1, SKU A | yes; those 3 units are not reimbursed again |
| 3 units, warehouse loss, adjustment 2, SKU A | no |
| 3 units, inbound shortage, a shipment, SKU A | no |

## Return-not-received timing (hypothetical)

A claim raised while the return wait after the buyer refund is still running is too early; a claim raised after the return claim window has closed is too late; and a restock of that order bars the claim whenever the restock is dated.

## Valuation illustration (hypothetical cost and cap)

4 units with a declared unit cost of 600.00 USD, under a cap of 500.00 USD, are reimbursed at 500.00 USD each, 2000.00 USD in all.
